For the reaction in equilibrium
$\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{~g})+3 \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{~g}), \Delta \mathrm{H}=-\mathrm{Q}$
Reaction is favoured in forward direction by:
options: low pressure, high temperature and high concentration of ammonia
high pressure, low temperature and higher concentration of $\mathrm{H}_2$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{N}_2(\mathrm{~g})+3 \mathrm{H}_2(\mathrm{~g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{NH}_3(\mathrm{~g}), \Delta \mathrm{H}=-\mathrm{Q}$
According to Le Chatelier's principle.
- Exothermic reactions are favoured at low temperature.
- Increase in pressure shifts the reaction in direction having lesser number of moles. Hence, the given reaction shifts forward on increasing pressure.
- Increasing the concentration of reactants shifts the reaction in forward direction. So high concentration of $\mathrm{H}_2$ shifts reaction in forward direction.

questions.solution: The correct answer is option (3) as mammals have the ability to produce a concentrated urine. The Henle's loop and vasa recta play a significant role in this. The flow of filtrate in the two limbs of Henle's loop as well as flow of blood through the two limbs of vasa recta are in a counter current pattern. The proximity between the Henle's loop and vasa recta, as well as the counter current in them help in maintaining the increasing osmolarity towards the inner medullary interstitium, i.e., from 300 mOsmol $\mathrm{L}^{-1}$ in the cortex to about $1200 \mathrm{mOsmol}^{-1}$ in the inner medulla. questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Select the correct statements regarding mechanism of muscle contraction.
A. It is initiated by a signal sent by CNS via sensory neuron.
B. Neurotransmitter generates action potential in the sarcolemma.
C. Increased $\mathrm{Ca}^{++}$level leads to the binding of calcium with troponin on action filaments.
D. Masking of active site for actin is activated.
E. Utilising the energy from ATP hydrolysis to form cross bridge.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: The correct answer is option (1) as muscle contraction is initiated by a signal sent by the CNS via a motor neuron. A neural signal reaching the neuromuscular junction releases a neurotransmitter (acetylcholine) which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma. This spreads through the muscle fibre and causes the release of $\mathrm{Ca}^{2 *}$ into the sarcoplasm. Increase in $\mathrm{Ca}^{2+}$ level leads to the binding of calcium with a subunit of troponin on actin filaments and thereby remove the masking of active sites for myosin. Utilising the energy from ATP hydrolysis, the myosin head now binds to the exposed active sites on actin to form a cross bridge.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following graphs depicts the effect of substrate concentration on velocity of enzyme catalysed reaction?
questions.solution:
Option (1) is the correct answer because with the increase in substrate concentration, the velocity of enzymatic reaction rises at first. The reaction ultimately reaches maximum velocity $\left(\mathrm{V}_{\max }\right)$ which is not exceeded by any further rise in concentration of the substrate. This is because the enzyme molecules are fewer than substrate molecules and after saturation of these molecules, there are no free enzyme molecules to bind the additional substrate molecules
Option (2) is incorrect as velocity of reaction is continuously increasing in the given graph. In option (3) after reaching at $\mathrm{V}_{\text {max }}$, velocity declines while in option (4) velocity of reaction declines from high on increasing substrate concentration. So, option (3) and (4) are incorrect.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Enzymes that catalyse the removal of groups from substrates by mechanisms other than hydrolysis leaving double bonds, are known as :
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (4) because lyases are group of enzymes that catalyse the removal of groups from substrates by mechanisms other than hydrolysis leaving double bonds.
Option (1) is incorrect because transferases are enzymes catalysing a transfer of a group G (other than hydrogen) between a pair of substrate S and $\mathrm{S}^{\prime}$.
Option (2) is incorrect because oxidoreductases are enzymes which catalyse oxidoreduction between two substrates S and $\mathrm{S}^{\prime}$.
Option (3) is incorrect because dehydrogenases are also known as oxidoreductases.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q:
Which of the following are correct about EcoRI?
A. Cut the DNA with blunt end
B. Cut the DNA with sticky end
C. Recognise a specific palindromic sequence
D. Cut the DNA between the base G and A when encounters the DNA sequence 'GAATTC'
E. Exonuclease

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option (4) as
EcoRI does not cut the DNA with blunt ends. Instead, it cuts the DNA with sticky / cohesive / staggered ends on each strand.
EcoRI is a restriction endonuclease that recognises a specific palindromic sequence and cuts at a specific site within the DNA, known as the restriction site. It is not an exonuclease as exonucleases remove nucleotides from the free ends of the DNA.
The recognition sequence for EcoRI is $\begin{aligned} & 5^{\prime}-\mathrm{G}^{\downarrow}-\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{C}-3^{\prime} \\ & 3^{\prime}-\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{A}_{\uparrow}-\mathrm{G}-5^{\prime}\end{aligned}$ and it cuts the DNA between bases G and A only when the sequence GAATTC is present in the DNA.
Therefore, 'A' and ' $E$ ' represent incorrect features about EcoRI, whereas ' B ', 'C' and ' D ' are correct features of EcoRI.
The other options, i.e., (1), (2) and (3) are incorrect as they represent incorrect combinations of features w.r.t. EcoRI.

D. Treatment with Taq polymerase and deoxynucleotides

That is $\mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{D} \rightarrow \mathrm{E} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}$
Option (2), (3) and (4) are incorrect as they represent incorrect sequence.
